title: A scheduled flow run skips a screen whose required field is named `schedule`, `jobId` or `flowName`: the schedule trigger's own params are read as the caller's answers
body:
**Class:** a (pre-existing on `main`). Found by the #19846 dev while enumerating every producer of an `AutomationContext` (PR #19899). It is outside that PR's scope, so it was not fixed there.

## What happens

The schedule trigger starts a run with platform seeds in `params` and no record:

- `packages/triggers/trigger-schedule/src/schedule-trigger.ts:806-810` on `origin/main`: `params: { jobId, flowName: binding.flowName, schedule }`.

A screen node on a headless run asks whether the caller already supplied each field (`callerSupplied` in `packages/services/service-automation/src/screen-input-contract.ts`). With no explicit signal from the producer, that verdict is inferred from `params`. The inference only rules out the row-id seeds the action and trigger doors write, so the schedule trigger's three keys count as caller answers.

## Measured (the #19846 dev, one-time probe on the real engine; not committed)

`engine.execute` on a `type: 'schedule'` flow, with the schedule trigger's context shape and a screen with a required field named `schedule`:
- **observed:** the run completes, output `{ schedule: '0 2 * * *' }`, and the screen never pauses;
- **expected:** the run pauses at the screen.

The seat has read the seeding code cited above. The probe run itself is the dev's.

## Property wanted

A scheduled run's platform seeds never answer a screen field. PR #19899 adds an explicit producer signal, `AutomationContext.callerParamKeys`, which the schedule trigger does not set. The card doesn't prescribe how to close this.

Dedupe words: schedule trigger screen skipped; callerParamKeys schedule; jobId flowName schedule params screen; headless screen inference scheduled run.
